messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: [P1] kvcache OOM pattern detected in hosted-runtime-prod (svc: inference-hosted-3). Metric: kvcache.evictions spike -> OOMs on 3/12 nodes. Auto-pager triggered. More details: https://grafana/redwood/d/kvcache

alice_oncall: acked. I'm looking. which clusters/regions affected?

bob_runtime: seeing enrich logs: continuous-batcher is growing windows for some sessions with long prompts — KV map size per request up 6x. probable runaway prefetched prefixes. grabbing live kvcache dump now.

carol_sre: running quick query to confirm. query I used:```
# quick gcloud / promql snippets
sum by(instance) (increase(kvcache_kv_count_total[5m]))
sum by(instance) (increase(process_resident_memory_bytes{job="hosted-runtime"}[5m]))
```

carol_sre: output -> instances a, b, c show +3.1M keys in last 5m, memory trending to 95% of container limit. evictions not keeping up.

bob_runtime: the continuous batch estimator mis-classified several sessions as short (so it kept delaying flush) and prefetch kept appending context. End result: huge KV maps and then OOM on allocate. I can repro locally with a long prompt + streaming enabled.

dan_support: are customers impacted? any 5xx/error spikes?

carol_sre: yes, api_5xx_rate for hosted inference routes increased from ~0.2% to 4.6% for the last 8m in us-west1. latency also spiked.

frank_cs: flagged two enterprise customers (acme-corp, clickly) — they reported chat failures and long hangs. CS oncall got inbound tickets. no immediate data exfil.

alice_oncall: immediate plan: 1) throttle prefetch/continuous-batcher aggressiveness (runtime config flip) 2) temporarily cap max KV per session to avoid OOM 3) add emergency eviction watermark to force cleanup 4) notify customers + PS. Who can flip runtime flags?

bob_runtime: I can push a runtime config hotflip to hosted control plane: set continuous_batch.max_delay_ms from 200 -> 30, continuous_batch.max_size from 32 -> 8, and kvcache.session_max_keys from 5_000_000 -> 200_000. That should stop growth quickly. Note: may cost slight throughput.

deploy-bot: deploy plan created: hotfix/3071112223/kvcache-firebreak (1 commit). Rolling config apply to hosted-runtime-prod (3 zones) with 2-min health checks.

alice_oncall: good, please apply and watch. Carol, can you prepare a scoped rollback if health degrades?

carol_sre: watch set up. I have an alert that will trigger if 5xx > 1% for >2m post-change. I'll also tail logs for OOM traces and eviction counts.

bob_runtime: pushing hotflip now. command:```
# runtimectl apply-config --env=prod --patch '{"continuous_batch": {"max_delay_ms": 30, "max_size": 8}, "kvcache": {"session_max_keys": 200000}}'
```

bob_runtime: applied to us-west1-1 -> ok, us-west1-2 -> ok, us-west1-3 -> ok. Deploy stopped at 3/3 healthy checks passing.

carol_sre: post-change metrics (2m later): kvcache_kv_count_total delta down 85% on affected nodes, memory pressure falling. api_5xx_rate trending back toward baseline. Good signal.

alice_oncall: great. Can we also enable a temporary route-level rate-limit for the top offending API key(s) that are sending long contexts? helps stop repeat offenders while we investigate.

emma_product: we should page product infra team about whether to adjust streaming heuristics longer term. Also recommend a change in default continuous-batcher config for hosted tier.

frank_cs: sending customer note draft to Alice: "We're aware of intermittent 5xx/responses; we've applied a mitigation that reduces latency and errors. We're following up with root cause and will share timeline for fixes." Want to publish to status page?

alice_oncall: yes, put a quick status note: "Degraded responses for hosted inference in us-west1 resolved after mitigation. Investigating root cause. No data loss." Keep minimal. Dan, please post with incident id INC-3071112223.

dan_support: posted status: https://status.redwood.ai/INC-3071112223. Also responding to open tickets and offering dedicated channel.

bob_runtime: follow-up checks: I grep'd logs and saw a pattern where 'system:prompt:chunked' with large user-generated prefixes consistently triggered the batching increase. sample snippet:```
[WARN] session=abc123 estimated_delay=180ms queued_tokens=0 -> continuous_batch delayed -> prefetch appended 512k tokens
[ERROR] kvcache: allocation failed: requested 120M keys
```

carol_sre: I dumped a small kvcache sample and found many stale entries tied to aborted sessions. Eviction wasn't evicting because policy relied on last-access and the prefetch path kept touching keys. We'll need to change eviction to account for aborted/session-state flags.

alice_oncall: action items while live: 1) runtime telemetry team to add an immediate metric for per-session-kv-growth-rate (bob) 2) SRE to add eviction-for-abort flag to kvcache (carol) 3) Product to review streaming/prefetch defaults (emma) 4) CS to track customer impact and escalation (frank) 5) Postmortem owner? volunteer?

bob_runtime: I'll own the telemetry metric and follow-up PR. I'll also instrument a short circuit: if session_kv_count > session_max_keys -> reject further prefetch and mark session read-only. quick PR in review: https://git.redwood/pr/4823

carol_sre: I'll file a low-risk change to eviction to consider session aborted bit and increase eviction aggressiveness under memory pressure.

emma_product: I'll schedule a sync with runtime to discuss heuristics and default knobs. Also want to discuss whether hosted should have a stricter default session_max_keys.

frank_cs: CS will reach out to the two impacted customers with technical notes and offer a post-incident call. I've captured Affected: acme-corp, clickly; Impact: 4-6% request failures and latency spikes over 10m window.

alice_oncall: handing off to night oncall in 2 hours. Summary for handoff: mitigation applied (batch caps + session_max_keys). System stable, memory pressure decreased, 5xx back toward baseline. Open follow-ups: PR 4823 (runtime short-circuit), SRE eviction change, telemetry metric, postmortem. Please keep incident open until RCA published.

deploy-bot: hotfix/3071112223/kvcache-firebreak merged and rolled.

bob_runtime: small note — hotfix reduces throughput headroom; we should expect slight increase in token cost for some workloads. I'll scope a canary for a smarter batching estimator (instead of hard caps) in next sprint.

alice_oncall: thanks all. If anything regresses ping @alice_oncall directly. handing off to @carol_sre for overnight watch.

carol_sre: taking over for night watch. My checkpoints: alarms for OOM traces, 5xx > 1% alert, kvcache_kv_count > 300k per instance. I'll update morning runbook and coordinate RCA doc.

frank_cs: done — customers notified, offered follow-up.

emma_product: adding incident to roadmap discussion.

alice_oncall: closing live mitigation loop. Will prepare draft timeline and start postmortem doc tomorrow. Thanks team :clap:
